description: Lock user accounts after a configurable number of consecutive failed authentication attempts, preventing online brute force and dictionary attacks. On Linux, pam_faillock (RHEL 8+) or pam_tally2 (legacy) tracks per-user authentication failures and locks the account when the threshold is reached. Key parameters: deny (max failed attempts, typically 5), unlock_time (lockout duration in seconds, typically 900), and fail_interval (window for counting failures). With deny=5 and unlock_time=900, brute force is rate-limited to approximately 20 attempts per hour per account, making password guessing computationally infeasible against any password meeting basic quality requirements. On Windows, equivalent policy is configured via Group Policy (Account Lockout Policy) or Fine-Grained Password Policies. Does not protect against password spraying (one password across many accounts) or credential stuffing with breached passwords — those require complementary controls like IP-based rate limiting and credential breach monitoring.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Without lockout, an attacker can make unlimited authentication attempts against a login interface (SSH, RDP, web console), enabling dictionary attacks and brute force with tools like Hydra or Medusa. With pam_faillock configured (deny=5, unlock_time=900), authentication is rate-limited to approximately 20 attempts per hour per account — making brute force of any password meeting basic quality requirements computationally infeasible. The attacker must find an alternative authentication bypass rather than simply guessing credentials. Note: per-account lockout does not prevent password spraying (one password across many accounts) or cause attacker-triggered denial-of-service by deliberately locking accounts — complementary controls (IP-based rate limiting, spray detection) address those scenarios

verification.method: Verify account lockout enforcement via pam_faillock (Linux) or Group Policy (Windows)

steps.description: Configure faillock.conf with deny=5 (lock after 5 failures), unlock_time=900 (15 min lockout), fail_interval=900 (failure counting window)
steps.command:
printf 'deny = 5
unlock_time = 900
fail_interval = 900
even_deny_root
root_unlock_time = 60
dir = /var/run/faillock
audit
silent
' > /etc/security/faillock.conf

steps.description: Ensure pam_faillock is enabled in system-auth and password-auth via authselect (RHEL 8+)

remediation.name: Windows account lockout policy via net accounts

steps.description: Set account lockout threshold to 5 failed attempts
Set lockout observation window to 30 minutes
